content.text:
I submitted index 8 (Sb fraction 0.43) as the best composition. At 0.00562% it had the highest EQE of the five I measured, about 50% above any other point. All five EQE measurements were used, plus 4 of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) | XRD phases |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.31 | 0.00301 | Mostly a copper-rich phase |
| 8 | 0.43 | **0.00562** | Mix of CuSb₂O₆ and a copper-rich phase |
| 9 | 0.46 | 0.00364 | Not measured |
| 12 | 0.56 | 0.00336 | CuSb₂O₆ only |
| 16 | 0.69 | 0.00345 | Not measured |
| 22 | 0.83 | Not measured | Antimony oxides |

I skipped the Sb-rich end on the basis of its XRD: index 22 showed antimony oxides, and EQE was already low by 0.69.

The best compositions seem to be where CuSb₂O₆ and a copper-rich phase coexist. Neither single-phase side did as well. The peak looks narrow: moving from 0.43 to 0.46 cut EQE by about a third. So the true best on the line may well be next to index 8 rather than at it. Indices 5–7 (0.34–0.40) are the likeliest unmeasured spot, and a few more EQE measurements there would settle it.
